I enjoy the game. It can be a bit grindy and repetitive, but lets be honest we knew what we were getting into when we bought it.
It's slop but it's good slop.
Mindless, grindy, and a 100-floor run can take you over 7 hours. If that sounds like fun, grab it on sale.

Only played a little bit so far but am looking forward to playing more. It's such a simple game, almost plays like an indie-rogue like, but the core gameplay feels decent. The movement isn't great but it's fluid enough, the enemies' attacks are mostly well communicated and the aiming is alright. There's a good selection of weapons and upgrades too. The enemies are kind of repetitive but there is some variety. The overall theme of labor exploitation is appreciated and overt, and I do really hope that the opening statement of the game not being made in an exploitative working environment is true.

So, the art style is fantastic. It's bright, cheery, over-the-top, ridiculous, and heavily stylized in a great way. The voice acting is amazing too, every single voice actor is clearly giving it their all! But it has to be said that the game absolutely objectifies almost all of the women and girls in it. The two main PCs are literally dressed as schoolgirls but are obviously sexualized. And the dialogue present in the "augmentation" upgrade segments is really off-putting and weird. This is really gross and not okay, but this sort of disturbing stereotype is completely and deeply a part of a lot of anime and anime art-styles. I kind of get that this game is going to be geared towards teenage gooners and incels who just don't care about probably anyone else, but I feel like these things should still be pointed out and I would prefer to play games without these kinds of things. 

I love how the lady with the huge honkers has bandaids on her cleavage though, kind of genius ngl

Okay, I beat the game, it was actually pretty fun. It gets repetitive past like, sixty floors, but what they've created here actually works. I would play a more complex version of this game, like if they made a sequel with a bigger budget I would absolutely buy it and play da heck out of it.
pretty fun game but does get really really repetitive i wouldnt say its worth the asking price but a sale may be the way to go

I need to start with, this is a AA release and I am judging it on it's sale price. It's worth $10, and not more than that.
3D roguelike with anime girls that is a really rough diamond. It's gameplay loop is compelling, and it has enough weapon variety that it rewards the player by not just choosing stats. You are trying to get to floor 100, while livestreaming and chat occasionally giving challenges for superchat money. If you die, you can travel back with a single use key to various floor, so for instance if you get to floor 55, you get a key back to that floor, but if you go to floor 55 on your next run, and then die, you lose the key and will have to use one for either a lower or higher floor. While the character design might scream fanservice, the game does not have any that I saw without DLC. It's all competent, and is a great base for a game.

Now to the bad parts. The game itself has a good foundation, but nothing is built on it. The livestream thing, has nothing from it. You don't interact from chat, or seem to care about chat in any way. The developers need to either expand it, or cut it, but where it's at, it's the most blatant of napkin ideas that never got fleshed out.
The key system is a good idea, but they are few between and basically it's a massive punishment if you die twice in a row. But it gets worse, this is a roguelike, so smarter players will never use their higher level keys, because you need to build up your arsenal so you don't get smoked because you don't have any mods.
But you earn stuff right, so the game gets easier right? Not really. The mods you buy is energy and HP basically, the only damage upgrades you get is inside the dungeon, so when you restart on level 1, you feel the same as level 100. You never feel overpowered, it makes it feel really like a full restart because your praying for RNG to not screw you.
The  tower is lonely. You occasionally mention chat in passing, or talk to science girl briefly, but there is no lore in this game. You just run from floor entrance to floor exit. There is a merchant room, but no merchant. It needs something to carry you, and it lacks it. In a game that is asking you to do the same thing alot, you need something to latch onto.
The fanservice, clearly the game is ashamed of it, but uses it as a selling point. It feels combative. How dare you look at our game, that we chose the character designs for, creep. This is probably because of a worldwide audience, and maybe the lines judging the player could be chalked up to localizers being garbage at their job.

At the end of the day, the story is bad and half baked, the tower needs something to break up the monotony, and the roguelike elements don't work because the overwhelming majority is for survivability, meaning that it's going to take you the nearly the same length of time with all upgrades, as with no upgrades. The various tower drops (reset on death) do make different playstyles when you start experimenting, and there is alot to play around with.
It's a 5.5, that on sale could be a fun weekend, but can easy to burn yourself out on, it needs something more than trap room, reward room, normal fight room, and merchant room. Get it on sale if you like these kinda games, I probably won't finish a new game plus cycle.
